title: What You Must Tell ATC
hook: Some silence is golden. This silence is a violation.

scenes.narration: Cleared to nine thousand, but the summer air is thin and the airplane's giving you four hundred feet a minute. Tops. You're quiet, ATC's quiet. Kid — one of you is required to speak.
Four hundred feet a minute is all you've got. Required report — yes or no? Commit.
Yes. Can't make five hundred a minute — report it. Why? ATC's separation math assumes you climb like you said you would. When you can't, their picture is wrong and only you know it.

The rest of the always list: leaving an assigned altitude. A missed approach. True airspeed off five percent or ten knots. Altitude changes V F R on top. Entering or leaving a hold. And anything broken — confession is free, the ramp check isn't.
Off radar, add two: position at compulsory reporting points, and an E T A off by more than three minutes. Yes kid, we did that every day. Uphill. Both ways.
Eyes off the screen. Name four always-required reports. I'll sip while you think.
Altitude changes. Missed approaches. Speed changes. Holds. Broken stuff. Can't climb five hundred. When in doubt, key up — nobody ever failed a checkride for talking too politely.
From the altitudes lesson — M O C A guarantees nav signal within how many miles? Quick.
A I M five dash three dash three. The full guest list.

quiz.question: Cleared to climb but only able to manage 400 fpm. You must:
choices: Report being unable to climb at least 500 fpm
Nothing — climb rate isn't ATC's business
quiz.explanation: An average climb/descent rate below 500 fpm is on the always-report list — ATC's separation assumes standard rates. (AIM 5-3-3)

quiz.question: You must report a change in average true airspeed of:
quiz.explanation: A TAS change of 5% or 10 knots (whichever is greater) from what's filed must be reported.

quiz.question: A report required only when NOT in radar contact:
choices: Position over each compulsory reporting point
quiz.explanation: Compulsory position reports (and ETA changes >3 min) apply in a non-radar environment; the others are always required.
